record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present, including appendices. No apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests next-token-trained models on a lookahead path-finding task and reports a local teacher-forced shortcut alongside failure to solve the task. This refines and challenges claims of planning from ordinary next-token training; its teacherless results use a deliberately changed objective.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses rhyming and story-writing conceptually but reports no rhyme experiment. It cites future-token recovery from hidden states by other work and explicitly says this does not establish good planning; those cited results are not this study's results. The teacherless objective replaces answer-prefix inputs with dummy tokens and is intended to force lookahead, so its success is not evidence that ordinary next-token models show that behavior without inducement. Reversed-path results are discussed as a comparator and are not included as rows here.
record.test_reason: On a path-star task that requires look-ahead, teacher-forced Transformers and Mamba score at chance on the first, goal-dependent node. Meanwhile they almost perfectly follow whatever neighbour they are fed. This is the study's own evidence that next-token training yields a local shortcut rather than a plan (V6), and that look-ahead fails to emerge in this task (V5). Teacherless training deliberately forces look-ahead, so it counts as induced and is not evidence on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors argue the failure comes from teacher-forced training (a Clever Hans shortcut that leaves the first token indecipherable), not from autoregressive inference or architecture. It appears in both Transformers and Mamba, in-distribution. Teacherless and reversed training avoid it in some settings, and teacherless training lets GPT2-Large solve most graphs. Extension to story-writing and ordinary text is speculative.
record.recipe_differences: The paper's central experiment is a custom path-star task, not the rhyme-word intervention described in the claim. It compares standard teacher-forcing with a teacherless dummy-token objective and reversed targets; it does not use rhyme probes or edits.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary by model, graph degree and path length, and training objective. GPT2-Large teacherless accuracy is high on several graph settings but 0.0 on G2,20 and G20,5; the from-scratch teacherless models mostly report 0.0. Standard performance is near the stated 1/d guessing level, with GPT2-Large at 3.5 on G20,5.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a deliberately teacherless dummy-token objective, GPT2-Large solves most graphs and GPT-Mini solves G2,5. Later tokens are learned first, and the paper infers the solution is stored internally. Most from-scratch teacherless models fail.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An objective built to force multi-token prediction can induce look-ahead on some model and graph settings; this is not spontaneous planning under next-token training.

fits_no_version.finding: On 3-digit addition, teacherless training is more sample-efficient than standard training and slightly less than reversed training (figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A teacherless objective may improve sample efficiency over teacher-forcing on 3-digit addition.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The authors characterize their arguments as empirical and conceptual rather than formal proof. They do not test very large models such as Llama2 or Mistral, and acknowledge that they have not shown the proposed failures across general text-generation tasks. The experiments use a constructed graph task; the addition comparison is figure-only. No error bars or statistical uncertainty are reported. Teacherless results are uneven across models and graph settings.
record.rows_left_out: Reversed-path accuracy values in Table 4 and further snowballing-error results in Fig. 5 were not included because they compare other training orderings or address inference-time error accumulation rather than the claim versions cataloged here. The paper also reports the first-token plot with approximate 1/d accuracy, included as the aggregate row r49.

untested.parts: All: no rhyming verse, frontier model, or rhyme-word intervention.
All: no probing of future tokens from hidden states. Future Lens is only cited, with the comment that decodability does not imply good planning.
All: no test of features computed for later positions in ordinary next-token models. The teacherless 'stored solution' inference (Remark 2) is for an induced objective and is not measured internally.
All: no rhyme task, open-weight attribution graphs, or probes.
Chess, Sokoban and natural multi-step reasoning; internal (probe or intervention) measures of look-ahead; pretrained LLMs at scale.
Depth of plans in natural-language generation; apparent plans in large pretrained LLMs; internal mechanistic confirmation of the shortcut beyond the behavioural forced-neighbour test.

missing.what: GPT2-Large trained to predict only the first (goal-dependent) node scores about 1/d: 50.2, 50.4, 18.9, 10.4 and 4.5%. Look-ahead is not learned even when the Clever Hans cheat is removed by truncation.

record.verdict_notes: Not an original source. GPT2-Large is pretrained but fine-tuned on the task; the other models are trained from scratch. All G20,5 teacher-forced results are confounded by failure to fit training data, so the reader's limits_scope label for them was dropped. Rows linked to both V5 and V6 carry a state judged against V6; for V5 the same rows mean look-ahead absent. The paper cites Future Lens, saying recoverable future tokens need not mean good planning, but reports no V2 data.

versions.untested_parts: No rhyming-verse test, candidate rhyme-word measurement, or intervention on rhyme words.
No measurement or probe of how far ahead a single hidden state predicts tokens. The discussion of future-token recovery refers to cited work.
No test of ordinary next-token models computing features at an earlier position for later positions, separate from next-token prediction.
No open-weight rhyme-planning test or attribution-graph/probing-tool analysis.
The experiments use path-star graph path-finding and an addition task, not multi-step reasoning, chess, or Sokoban; they do not directly measure internal look-ahead in those tasks.

The experiments test teacher-forced shortcuts and planning failure on the specified graph task, not the depth of plans in natural-language generation or the prevalence of such behavior in pretrained models generally.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Teacher-forced GPT-Mini, GPT2-Large and Mamba on G2,5, G2,20, G5,5 and G10,5
labels.reason: Approximately chance goal-path accuracy together with 95.9–100% forced-neighbour following supports a local shortcut in this condition group; Tables 1 and 2.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Teacher-forced small Transformers and Mamba trained on the synthetic path-star look-ahead task (G2,5–G10,5)
labels.reason: Failure under teacher forcing, alongside successful alternative training conditions, qualifies the tasks and training conditions in which look-ahead emerges. Reversed-path evidence is in Table 4, not r49.

relation.reason: Its own path-generation, forced-neighbour and training-objective experiments bear on planning failure and local shortcut use.

tranche.reason: The study supplies experimental counterexamples and a specific shortcut argument qualifying look-ahead claims under teacher-forced training.

source_check.notes: The supplied text is arXiv v3 dated 29 July 2025, with an ICML 2024 publication notice. Teacherless internal look-ahead is argued from task structure and learning curves, rather than demonstrated with internal probes.

statements.correction: r49: first-node accuracy approximately 1/d, Figure 4 left. Reversed-path accuracy: Table 4; GPT2-Large 99.6–99.9%; GPT-Mini 99.7–100% and Mamba 96.2–99.5% on the four named settings. First-node-only GPT2-Large: Table 5, approximately 1/d.
statements.problem: The accuracy values are correct, but r49 is not the reversed-path comparator.

statements.correction: Mamba: tested on path-star graphs; teacher-forced accuracy approximately chance on G2,5, G2,20, G5,5 and G10,5, Table 2. Other non-transformer architectures are not tested by this study.
statements.problem: Mamba belongs to a tested negative condition, so non-transformer models other than DRC cannot collectively be called untested.

statements.correction: Two architectural families: Transformer and Mamba; three model configurations: GPT-Mini, GPT2-Large and Mamba. Controls/comparisons: teacherless objective, reversed targets, supplied-first-node evaluation, first-node-only training; §5.1 and §§F.1–F.5. No uncertainty estimates accompany the listed table values.
statements.problem: Three model configurations are described as three architectures, and the statement incorrectly says there are no controls.

statements.correction: GPT2-Large: pretrained, 36 layers, fine-tuned and tested. Untested very large models: Llama2 and Mistral, explicitly noted in §A. No internal probing of the shortcut or empirical natural-language planning-depth measurement.
statements.problem: The exclusion of large pretrained LLMs is too broad: pretrained GPT2-Large is tested.

statements.correction: Teacher-forced models: approximately chance exact-path accuracy on the named settings, Table 2; supplied-neighbour path-following 95.9–100%, Table 1. No measured few-token planning horizon. Successful teacherless settings demonstrate dependence on training objective.
statements.problem: Chance-level path-star performance supports shortcut use and failure to plan, but does not establish a planning horizon of a few tokens.

statements.correction: Three model configurations across two architectural families. Controls/comparisons present: changed objective, reversed targets, supplied-first-node evaluation and first-node-only training. Reversed-path results: Table 4; r49 concerns first-node accuracy. The 95.9–100% forced-neighbour range spans Table 1's named model/settings; r16 alone is GPT-Mini G2,5 at 99.7%. No internal probes or uncertainty estimates for the listed table values.
statements.problem: The statement miscounts architectural families, denies existing controls, and cites r49 for reversed-path results.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Standard teacher-forced path-star experiments, G2,5 through G10,5, and forced-neighbor tests on those graph settings
reader_labels.reason: Exact-path accuracy is at or near the stated random-guessing level while forced-neighbor path-following is 95.9–100%; the paper interprets the latter as a shortcut that fits later tokens without solving the goal-directed task (r01–r04, r06–r09, r11–r14, r16–r19, r21–r24, r26–r29).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: G20,5 forced-neighbor tests and GPT2-Large standard G20,5
reader_labels.reason: The shortcut test is 0.0 for all three models on G20,5, and the paper notes that these models struggle to fit training data there; GPT2-Large's standard exact-match value is also 3.5 rather than the stated approximate 1/d (r05, r10, r15, r20, r25, r30).
